page.title: AI consultant vs automation agency: which to hire?
page.description: Compare scope, timeline, pricing and deliverables so you can decide between an AI consultant and an automation agency for your marketing ops.
page.h1: Should you hire an AI consultant or an automation agency?
page.definition: An AI consultant is a specialist who evaluates your data, recommends use cases, selects tools and builds a roadmap, while an automation agency delivers working integrations, scripts and ongoing support under a retainer. The consultant typically works on a day‑rate or fixed project basis, whereas the agency charges a build fee plus a monthly retainer.
page.quick_answer: If you need a strategic assessment and a prioritized list of AI use cases, hire a consultant; if you need production‑ready workflows, integrations and ongoing maintenance, engage an automation agency.

sections.h2: What scope does each partner cover?

blocks.p: A consultant defines the problem, audits data, recommends use cases, selects tools and hands you a roadmap, while an agency builds the automations, connects systems and provides ongoing support.

ul: Consultant: discovery workshops, data audit, use‑case prioritization, tool evaluation, roadmap document
Agency: workflow design, script development, API integration, testing, documentation, support retainer

sections.h2: How do timelines and dependencies differ?

blocks.p: Consultant engagements usually finish in a few weeks and depend on stakeholder availability for interviews, while agency builds run longer and require stable APIs, test environments and change‑management approvals.

ol: Consultant: kickoff, stakeholder interviews, data review, use‑case mapping, tool shortlist, roadmap delivery
Agency: requirements sign‑off, environment provisioning, prototype build, integration testing, user acceptance, go‑live, retainer start

sections.h2: Which pricing model fits your budget?

blocks.p: Consultants bill by day‑rate or fixed project, making cost predictable for a defined scope, whereas agencies charge a one‑time build fee plus a recurring retainer for maintenance and enhancements.

blocks.p: A consultant hands over a written assessment, a ranked use‑case list, a tool recommendation matrix and a phased roadmap, while an agency delivers working scripts, integration configs, test reports and a support handbook.

ul: Consultant deliverables: assessment report, prioritized use‑case list, tool comparison matrix, implementation roadmap
Agency deliverables: automation scripts, API connectors, configuration files, test results, run‑book, support SLA

sections.h2: When should you involve West Peek Productions?

blocks.p: West Peek Productions sets up human‑in‑the‑loop AI workflows for marketing, content and event teams and can produce virtual, hybrid and webinar events; bring them in when you need both strategic AI guidance and hands‑on production execution.

faq.q: Can a single provider act as both consultant and agency?
faq.a: Some firms offer a blended model where they first assess and then build, but the pricing and accountability structures differ; clarify whether the same team will own the roadmap and the production code before signing.

faq.q: How do I measure success after hiring an agency?
faq.a: Track automation run‑rate, error frequency, time saved per process and the number of new use cases shipped each quarter; tie these metrics to the retainer review cadence.

faq.q: What happens if the consultant’s roadmap changes after the agency starts building?
faq.a: Scope changes trigger a change‑request process; the agency will estimate impact on timeline and retainer cost, and both parties must approve before work continues.

faq.q: Do I need a separate project manager for the agency engagement?
faq.a: Agencies usually assign a technical lead, but a client‑side product owner or project manager helps prioritize backlog items, approve releases and communicate business changes.
